subject: FinBridge trial: technical bridge plan, API contract & eval rituals
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben.c@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.j@finbridge.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.p@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.i@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-07-15T14:05:00-07:00
Subject: FinBridge trial: technical bridge plan, API contract & eval rituals

Alex — great call this morning, thanks for walking through the platform use-case. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have alignment before the kickoff: 

Summary of needs
- Real-time customer chat summarization and policy-safe action suggestions (tool-calling to internal ticketing)
- ~500k tokens/month during the POC; peak QPS expectation ~6 rps with 256-token avg responses
- Acceptable p95 inference latency <= 350ms for the critical path; looking to measure cost economics per 1k messages

Proposed success criteria (draft)
1) Functional: model outputs hit >= 85% precision on your moderation prompt set (we'll use your 100-case eval suite)
2) Performance: p95 end-to-end <= 350ms on hosted endpoint for 99% of sampling windows
3) Cost: baseline token cost below your threshold (we'll instrument token breakdown during the POC)
4) Integration: SDK route and streaming integration completed with one canary route and automated fallback

Technical asks to unblock the POC
- Provide a sandbox API key and a small sample of the event payloads (anonymized).
- Confirm whether the ticketing integration supports an async webhook or requires tool-calling via an authenticated RPC.
- Security/compliance contact for a brief checklist exchange (SOC2 scope items).

Proposed POC timeline (6 weeks)
- Week 0 (this week): scope confirmation, sandbox creds, data access
- Week 1: SDK integration and streaming PoC (Monica owns delivery)
- Week 2–3: Test harness + eval run (Karthik to coordinate metrics and rollout gating)
- Week 4–5: Acceptance testing, canary, and cost/latency regression review
- Week 6: Final review and handoff to production plan

Attachments: attached a one-page scope (finbridge_poc_scope.xlsx) — small workbook with suggested eval cases.

Next steps
- Can you confirm the sandbox key and point person for compliance by EOD Friday?
- If you agree with the draft success criteria I listed, we'll lock the acceptance tests into the Runbook.

Thanks — looking forward to getting started.

—
Ben Carter
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
ben.c@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0198

Also looping in: can your streaming approach support chunked partial responses with tool calls invoked mid-stream? That's one of our key UX asks (we don't want the agent to block the UI while waiting for a tool response).

I'll also attach the internal compliance checklist for your team to review.

Subject: Re: FinBridge trial: technical bridge plan, API contract & eval rituals

Alex — appreciate the quick turnaround and the checklist. Short answers to your streaming/tool-calling questions + implementation plan sketch: 

Streaming and tool-calling
- Redwood streaming supports chunked partial outputs and allows tool-calls to be emitted as structured events mid-stream. The client can render partial tokens while we schedule tool execution. When the tool returns, the stream resumes with the updated context.
- Pattern we recommend: ``prefetch + speculative partials`` — send the likely follow-up tokens while the tool executes, with a deterministic merge step to avoid hallucinated state.

Suggested API contract (initial)
- POST /v1/generate (sync) — for small synchronous calls (<= 1s expected).
- POST /v1/stream (streaming) — SSE/HTTP2 streaming with event types: data, tool_call, tool_result, done.
- POST /v1/tool/call (callback) — internal endpoint for tool execution acknowledgements (server-to-server webhook).

SDK integration notes
- We provide client SDKs (Node/Python) that wrap the stream and emit tool_call events to your ticketing endpoint. Monica will supply a sample route implementation for your webhook consumer on Monday.
- For KV cache: we'll use per-session KV that can be passed as a cache-id header to avoid re-priming long histories during the trial.

Telemetry and gating
- Karthik will own instrumentation: token-level cost, p95 latency, model confidence heatmaps, and false-positive rates on the eval set. We'll surface these in the POC dashboard and wire alerts for regressions.

I'll let Monica and Karthik follow up with concrete sprint tasks and a kickoff slot. Thanks again.

—
Ben Carter
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Alex / Ben — Monica here (Solutions Engineer). I've sketched a concrete sprint breakdown and owner assignments below plus the acceptance test checklist we'll run against your sample eval suite.

Sprint plan (Week 1–6)
- Week 0 (prep): FinBridge provides sandbox key + anonymized payloads; Redwood provides sample webhook receiver and a pre-configured SDK package. (Owner: Alex / Ben)
- Week 1 (integration): Integrate Node SDK, implement POST /v1/stream client; implement ticket webhook handler for tool_call events. (Owner: Monica)
- Week 2 (eval harness): Run 100-case labeled suite; record precision/recall and token costs. (Owner: Karthik)
- Week 3 (canary): Route 5% of traffic through streaming canary route; measure p95 and error budget. (Owner: Monica)
- Week 4 (regression): Tune batching/kv cache and re-run harness; document cost delta. (Owner: Karthik)
- Week 5–6 (acceptance + handoff): Acceptance review, ops playbook delivery, production path recommendations. (Owner: Ben / Monica)

Acceptance test checklist (will be automated where possible)
- Functional: 100 labeled cases run; target >= 85% precision on accept/reject; top-3 intent accuracy >= 90%
- Performance: streaming p95 <= 350ms, error rate < 1% on canary
- Cost: projected monthly token cost <= $X (we'll finalize after first eval run)
- Integration: tool_call -> ticket webhook end-to-end within 2s median; idempotency checks pass

Implementation details and constraints
- SDK route: we'll supply sample code for POST /v1/stream (Node) that handles event types and gracefully retries tool calls.
- Fallback: implement route-level fallback to a lighter quantized model for non-critical requests to preserve latency SLO during peaks.
- Security: we'll perform a brief boundary review (no customer PII in sample payloads). Karthik will track the checklist items and manage sign-offs.

Meeting cadence
- Weekly 30-minute standups for the first 3 weeks (Mon/Wed) and a 60-minute acceptance review at the end of Week 6. I'll send calendar invites after we confirm kickoff.

Attachments: sample SDK snippet and a compact test plan attached to this message for your engineers.

Next steps (action items)
- Alex: confirm sandbox key delivery + Samira as security contact (due: 2028-07-18)
- Ben: schedule kickoff (due: 2028-07-18)
- Monica/Karthik: post-provide the SDK sample and the harness template (due: 2028-07-19)

Happy to jump on a short technical call if the engineering teams want to walk the sample together.

—
Monica Patel
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
monica.p@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0234
